n: Complicit or infiltrated financial institutions and insiders
ds: Criminals gain access to the financial system by corrupting or recruiting staff, acquiring control of an institution, or using a counterparty institution whose own controls are weak or deliberately bypassed. Defensive focus is on spotting the signs at three levels: the individual insider, the institution's own governance and reporting, and counterparty institutions whose behaviour no longer matches their size and customer base.

src.t: FATF, Guidance on Correspondent Banking Services, 2016
Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, Sound management of risks related to money laundering and financing of terrorism, 2014 (revised 2020)

cn.rt: Cross-cutting risk factor; applies across all consumer products and channels. Insider complicity can touch any product or channel.

rat: Insider and counterparty-bank complicity; correspondent/respondent relationships and staff override.

ind.n: Staff override of controls or excessive record access
ind.cx: Staff bypass or override screening, monitoring or approval steps, or access records of customers outside their duties, for a particular set of customers.
ind.fp: Privileged roles and emergency fixes legitimately involve overrides; require documented approval.
ind.ds: Employees override approvals, alter records, access records without need or show unusual relationships with customers.

ind.n: Insider override of credit policy or unusual speed of approval
ind.cx: Credit, onboarding or exception approvals are pushed through unusually fast by the same employee, with thin verification, for connected customers.
ind.fp: May have innocent explanations; assess in context of customer profile and other indicators.
ind.ds: Staff-approved exceptions or rapid decisions with limited verification.

ind.cx: Employee or relative accounts receive payments from customers or vendors, a sign of bribes or commissions for favourable treatment.
ind.ds: Staff accounts credited from customers, vendors or dormant accounts.

ind.n: Screening alerts closed repeatedly for the same pattern with minimal rationale
ind.cx: Alerts on the same customers or pattern are closed repeatedly with minimal rationale, which may reflect an insider shielding activity.
ind.ds: Internal indicator of weak alert handling that may mask manipulation.

ind.cx: A correspondent or respondent institution is found to be offering access to undisclosed downstream banks or payment firms.
ind.fp: Group and agency arrangements are disclosed normally.
ind.ds: Respondent provides access to its account for other banks or payment firms (nesting) without disclosure.

ind.n: Transaction volumes disproportionate to respondent's size
ind.cx: A counterparty bank's flows are far beyond what its balance sheet and customer base can explain, suggesting it is being used as a conduit.
ind.ds: Flows far exceed expected levels for the respondent's balance sheet or footprint.

ind.n: Links to shell banks or unlicensed entities
ind.cx: A counterparty institution is found to deal with shell banks or unlicensed entities, or to be controlled by one.
ind.ds: Respondent has relationships with shell or unlicensed institutions.

ind.n: Institution ownership or control passes to opaque parties followed by a volume surge
ind.cx: Marks the point at which a previously sound institution may have been taken over to serve criminal flows.
ind.fp: Genuine acquisitions, recapitalisations and expansion strategies change ownership and volumes together. Verify the new owners' source of wealth and business plan.
ind.ds: A bank, payment firm or other regulated entity changes owners, directors or key managers to parties whose backing is unclear, and soon afterwards shows sharply higher volumes, new customer types or new corridors.

ind.n: Internal reporting on specific customers blocked, withdrawn or never raised
ind.cx: Core complicity sign, as the human reporting chain is the control being neutralised.
ind.fp: Reports may be legitimately closed after review or consolidated into one case. Look for patterns tied to one manager or portfolio.
ind.ds: Staff or managers discourage unusual-activity reports on a customer, reverse escalations, or reports for a particular relationship repeatedly fail to arrive at the compliance function.

ind.n: Manual entries through internal or suspense accounts hiding customer flows
ind.cx: Lets an insider move or conceal funds outside normal monitoring, and is usually found by audit or ledger analytics.
ind.fp: Operational corrections, reconciliations and settlement timing legitimately use internal accounts. Review ageing, authorisers and counterparties.
ind.ds: Funds move via manual journals, suspense, clearing or staff-controlled internal accounts, so customer-level records do not show the real origin, destination or beneficial party.

ctl.ds: Restricts and logs privileged and bulk access to customer and case systems and alerts on anomalous user activity. It deters insider misuse and leakage of sensitive investigations and customer data.

ctl.n: Segregation of duties and dual authorisation
ctl.ds: Ensures no single person can create, approve and release a payment or master-data change, requiring an independent second approver. It controls insider and impersonation fraud.

Provides protected, confidential channels for staff, workers and suppliers to report misconduct or concerns, together with conduct monitoring to surface insider collusion. It brings internal and supply-chain issues to light.
Verifies lender ownership, loan terms and rationale, collateral origin and repayment sources, and alerts on early or third-party repayment. It prevents loans being used to place or layer funds.

ctl.n: Sampling, quality assurance and analytics audit
ctl.ds: Takes periodic samples of customer files, alert decisions, relied-upon files or analytical datasets and tests them for exceptions, duplicates and errors, feeding findings back to owners and training. It independently confirms that controls work as designed.

Requires declarations of conflicts from staff and third parties with annual refresh, rotation of relationship managers and challenge of exceptions. It reduces the chance that decisions are shaped by personal interest.

Compares actual activity with the customer's declared profile, history and peers and alerts on material or trend-breaking deviation, usually as a contextual signal. It catches change that rules on fixed thresholds miss.

ctl.n: Alert adjudication standards and quality assurance
ctl.ds: Defines documented criteria for clearing or escalating screening and monitoring alerts, resolves matches using secondary identifiers and samples closed alerts for quality. It makes decisions consistent, defensible and auditable.
Requires respondents to disclose and approve downstream institutions and detects payment patterns that imply undeclared nested use. It limits exposure to unknown third-tier clients.

ctl.n: Periodic respondent review and volume monitoring
ctl.ds: Reviews respondent activity against expected volumes, updates expected activity and restricts routing via higher-risk banks. It keeps correspondent risk assessments current after onboarding.

Weights alert priority by the assessed risk of the counterparty and profiles counterparties that cannot be explained by the customer's business. It directs analyst attention to payments involving higher-risk parties.
Rules that alert on abnormal count, value or speed of movements over defined windows compared with customer profile and peer norms. They provide baseline coverage across many typologies.

ctl.n: Correspondent respondent due diligence and risk rating
ctl.ds: Assesses respondent banks' jurisdiction, ownership, regulation, products and AML controls at onboarding using questionnaires and risk rating, including counterparty bank review. It sets the basis for correspondent relationships.

Verifies licences, registrations and supervisory status of customers, agents and counterparties against regulator registers before onboarding and periodically. It confirms legal authority to operate and detects unlicensed activity.
Obtains and verifies attestations and checks registers to confirm counterparties are not shell banks lacking physical presence and supervision. It bars a high-risk category of relationship outright.

Identifies the natural persons who ultimately own or control a legal entity or arrangement and verifies them using independent registers and documents, looking through intermediate layers. It is the core defence against anonymity achieved through layered or opaque structures.

Applies additional information gathering, corroboration, monitoring and senior review to relationships or transactions assessed as higher risk, covering purpose, expected activity, ownership and funds. The depth is proportionate to the risk drivers identified.
Provides a simple internal reporting channel and feedback loop so front-line staff can escalate observations, pressure and cash-handling anomalies. It turns staff observations into cases for review.

ctl.n: Suspicious reporting timeliness and quality assurance
ctl.ds: Measures how quickly suspicious activity reports are filed after suspicion forms and subjects narratives to peer or second-line review for completeness and usefulness. Weak or late reports are corrected and root causes fed back to analysts, so intelligence reaches authorities on time and in a usable form.
